anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: The paper describes MNE-BIDS, a technical specification and tool for organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format, which is a general analysis method, not a description of the SINGSING dataset.

anchors.paper_title: MEG-BIDS, the brain imaging data structure extended to magnetoencephalography
anchors.reason: The paper proposes MEG-BIDS, a principled solution and standard for organizing and sharing MEG data, making it a technical specification/methodology rather than a paper describing the SINGSING dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Data were collected using simultaneous EEG and MEG recording during an auditory oddball protocol in which participants were presented with harmonic complex sound (HCS) stimuli varying in frequency. MEG data acquisition was performed at the MEG Centre (Timone Hospital, Marseille, France).

citation_details.title: Mismatch negativity as a neurophysiological biomarker differentiating non-suicidal self-injury from suicidal behavior in depressed adolescents
citation_details.author: Jiaren Zheng, Zhuanlin Lin, Yanting Lin, Ping Lin, Bo Zheng, Zhong Zheng, Peter Hong
citation_details.abstract:
BACKGROUND
Mismatch negativity (MMN), an electrophysiological index of pre-attentive prediction-error processing, is impaired in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, its utility in distinguishing adolescents with MDD who engage in non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) from those with suicidal behavior (SB) remains unclear.


METHODS
We recruited 228 adolescents (10-24 years) into four groups: healthy controls (HC), MDD-Only, MDD + NSSI, and MDD + SB (n = 57 each). MMN was recorded using a passive auditory frequency MMN paradigm. Early (100-200 ms) and late (> 200 ms) component latency and amplitude were analyzed via ANOVA, targeted analyses, and spatiotemporal cluster-based permutation tests.
